'''Charles Burton Thaxton''' (born 1939) is an American [[physical chemist]]. He is a proponent of [[special creation]] who went on to become one of the first [[Intelligent Design|intelligent design]] authors. 

He was a Fellow of the [[Discovery Institute]]'s [[Center for Science and Culture]],<ref name="Discovery Institute 2009" /> and is currently a Fellow of the Discovery Institute.<ref name="Discovery Institute 2023">{{cite web | title=Charles Thaxton | website=Discovery Institute | date=14 February 2023 | url=https://www.discovery.org/p/thaxton/ | access-date=14 February 2023}}</ref>

==Biography==
Thaxton earned his [[Ph.D.]] in [[physical chemistry]] from [[Iowa State University]] in 1970. His doctoral dissertation was titled, "A technique for cooling single crystals below 90 degrees K for X-ray and the crystal structures of dihydrogen hexa-tantalum octadecachloride-6-hydrate, and the photodimer of 1,1-dimethyl 2,5-diphenyl 1-silacyclopentadiene".<ref>{{Cite web |title=A technique for cooling single crystals below 90 degrees K for X-ray and the crystal structures of dihydrogen hexa-tantalum octadecachloride-6-hydrate, and the photodimer of 1,1-dimethyl 2,5-diphenyl 1-silacyclopentadiene |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/69f1ec548f912e0e10374d2853d36207/1?cbl=18750&diss=y&pq-origsite= |access-date=10 February 2025 |publisher=[[Proquest]] |type=PhD Thesis}}</ref> He went on to complete post-doctorate programs in the [[history of science]] at [[Harvard University]] and the [[molecular biology]] laboratories of [[Brandeis University]].<ref name="Discovery Institute 2009">[http://www.discovery.org/scripts/viewDB/index.php?command=view&isFellow=true&id=96 Charles Thaxton Biography] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090414231210/http://www.discovery.org/scripts/viewDB/index.php?command=view&id=96&isFellow=true |date=2009-04-14 }}, [[Discovery Institute]]</ref>

Thaxton has co-authored several books, including ''The Mystery of Life's Origin'' and ''The Soul of Science''.<ref name=matzke/> In ''The Mystery of Life's Origin'', Thaxton argues for "[[Special creation|Special Creation]] by a creator beyond the cosmos", and asserts that Special Creation holds "that the ''source that produced life'' was intelligent".<ref name=Forrestexpreport>{{cite web |url=http://www.creationismstrojanhorse.com/FORREST_EXPERT_REPORT.pdf |title=Expert Witness Report |author=Barbara Forrest |author-link=Barbara Forrest |date=April 1, 2007 |publisher=United States District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania |accessdate=2008-10-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081028220124/http://www.creationismstrojanhorse.com/FORREST_EXPERT_REPORT.pdf |archive-date=October 28, 2008 }}</ref>

He was the editor of the first edition of the [[intelligent design]] textbook, ''[[Of Pandas and People]]''.<ref name=matzke>{{cite news|publisher=[[National Center for Science Education]]|date=2006-10-25|url=http://www.ncseweb.org/resources/articles/9018_90__matzke_2006_the_story_10_3_2006.asp|title=9.0. Matzke (2006): The Story of the Pandas Drafts|author=Nick Matzke|access-date=2007-11-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013214505/http://ncseweb.org/resources/articles/9018_90__matzke_2006_the_story_10_3_2006.asp|archive-date=2007-10-13|url-status=dead}}</ref> The book was featured prominently in ''[[Kitzmiller v. Dover Area School District]]'' and the sequence of drafts that show the transition between the terms "creation" and "creator" to "design", "designer", and "intelligent design", proved important in the judge's decision.<ref>{{cite book |author=Humes, Edward |title=Monkey girl: evolution, education, religion, and the battle for America's soul |publisher=ECCO |location=New York, N.Y |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-06-088548-9 |page=[https://archive.org/details/monkeygirlevolut00hume/page/380 380] |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/monkeygirlevolut00hume/page/380 }}; see judge's decision, pp 331-332</ref>

Thaxton stated that he preferred intelligent design to [[creationism]] because he "wasn’t comfortable with the typical vocabulary that for the most part creationists were using because it didn’t express what I was trying to do. They were wanting to bring God into the discussion, and I was wanting to stay within the empirical domain and do what you can do legitimately there".<ref>Thaxton, C. "Deposition of Dr. Charles Thaxton, 53:5–11" (Kitzmiller v. Dover Area Sch. Dist, 400 F. Supp. 2d 707, M.D. Pa., July 19, 2005).</ref>

Thaxton and his wife, Carole Thaxton, founded the "KONOS Academy," which is a private Christian 1-12 school in [[Tyrone, Georgia]], United States.<ref name="KronosBio">{{cite news|publisher=KONOS Connection |date=2009-04-25|url=http://www.konos.org/ |title=What is KONOS? }}</ref> Konos celebrated its 20-year anniversary in December 2021. He also teaches at [[Charles University]] in Prague.{{Citation needed|reason=There is no mention of this - or any other - university at konos.org, nor in their about section.|date=April 2026}}
